messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Should RStan reject unknown arguments?
parts:
I don't know what the convention is in R, but failing
silently on "inits" rather than "init" seems confusing
for users.

An intermediate solution might be to provide a clear
warning, but my preference would be to just fail if that's
not too outrageous a behavior for R.

- Bob




On Aug 31, 2014, at 10:55 AM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:

> Hi Cody,
>
> I just looked at the RStan manual. It looks like the option is "init," not "inits."
>
> Can you try that and let us know if that works?
>
> Daniel
>
> On Aug 31, 2014 3:52 AM, "Cody Ross" <ctr...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
> Daniel,
>
> Thanks for the quick reply. It looks like the problem is not just that the inits are on unconstrained space as opposed to constrained space, but that the inits are being generated randomly on {-2,2} instead on of 0 in unconstrained space, or as I specify them. The model runs quickly, and I can see the two major modes if I run enough chains, but id like to have control of the inits.
>
>
>
